Reference Petition Under Section 18 Of The Land Acquisition Act 1894 Award:
(By The Court U/S 26 Of Land Acquisition Act- 1894 On Reference
Petition U/S 18 Of The Act):
1.

This reference under section 18 of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was sent to this
court by the Land Acquisition Collector qua Award No.01/2011-2012.

2.  As per the LAC Award, a large tract of land measuring 3822 sq. meters of village Azadpur, Delhi, was acquired by the Govt. for a public purpose i.e. "Construction of Grade Separator at Azadpur, under Planned Development of Delhi".
Notification under Section 4 of The Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'LA Act') was issued on 18.04.2007.
Declaration under Section 6 was made on 11.01.2008.

Thereafter, Award bearing no.
01/2011-2012/DC (NW) was announced by Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as LAC) on 05.05.2011.
The LAC determined the market price of the acquired land as Rs.16,613/- per square meter.
LAC No. 154/17 page 2 of 7 SIDHARTH by SIDHARTH  MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.10.08  14:31:48 +0530 3.
The petitioner being dissatisfied with the market value determined by the LAC, filed the present petition u/s 18 of the LA Act, seeking reference to this court.
The Land Acquisition Collector forwarded the same to this court, for adjudication.

4. The petitioner's case in brief is that the petitioner was the owner /occupant and was in possession of the land bearing Khasra numbers as mentioned in the Statement u/s 19 of the LA Act that was annexed with the present reference and admitted by the petitioner during the stage of admission/denial of documents, situated within the of Village Azadpur, Delhi (the said land).
The said land was acquired vide notification dated 18.04.2007.

5. The petitioner has challenged the said award inter alia on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and incorrect assessment of market value of land inter-alia due to non-consideration of relevant factors like potentiality and fertility of the suit land, the surrounding colonies and developed areas, the market value of the adjoining areas /villages, the sale deeds of other lands of the contemporary period, nearness to the National Highway and industrial areas, the amenities available in the suit land etc.
6.

The petitioner has prayed compensation at enhanced LAC No. 154/17 page 3 of 7 SIDHARTH by SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.10.08 14:31:54 +0530 rate besides interest thereon Kaushalya Devi vs Union Of India And Ors on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56346728/
2 and solatium in addition to the compensation.
7.

sentences.text: WS was not filed.
Accordingly, opportunity to file WS was closed on 21.05.2018.

8. In evidence, the counsel for petitioner has relied upon the judgment in a case Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI, LAC No. 38/17 DOD- 07.05.2025 and also the evidence led in said case.
9.

entities.text: Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI, LAC No. 38/17 DOD- 07.05.2025
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent no.1/Union of India, in its evidence, tendered the award as Ex. R1 in evidence.

The beneficiary department has adopted the evidence led on behalf of UOI/R-1.
10.
I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also carefully considered the record.

My issue-wise findings are given as under:-
FINDINGS ON ISSUE NO. 1 :-
11.
Petitioner has contended that valuation of land determined by LAC is not reasonable as LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
However, he has not led any evidence to show as to how the LAC was wrong in fixing market value of land.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has only relied upon the judgment titled as Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI & Anr., LAC No. 38/17, decided LAC No.
154/17 page 4 of 7 SIDHARTH by SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR

entities.text: Jai Bhagwan Gupta Vs. UOI & Anr., LAC No. 38/17
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Date: 2025.10.08 14:32:02 +0530 by Sh. Deepak Dabas, Ld.
Predecessor of this Court on 07.05.2025 conceded that award be passed in terms of the said judgment and the same enhancement which was granted in the said judgment be also granted to petitioner.
12. In Jai Bhagwan Gupta's case (Supra), an elaborate and detailed discussion was made before determining the amount of compensation.

With respect to the land of the village Azadpur (involved herein), acquired through the same notification (as made herein), the Ld. Predecessor of this Court determined the market value of the land as Rs. 27,000/- per square meter.

13. Since, no different evidence has been led by the petitioner in the present case, I have no reason to give a different treatment to the land of the petitioner and to give a determination, different from that determined in the Jai Bhagwan Gupta's case (Supra).
The fair market value of the acquired land is adjudicated as Rs. 27,000/- per square meter as determined in Jai Bhagwan Gupta's case (Supra).
Accordingly, I hold that the petitioner would be entitled to market value @ Rs. 27,000/- per square meter.
14. Petitioner has also claimed compensation for crops, tree, tubewell etc.

However, the petitioner has failed to lead any evidence to substantiate his claim or to establish LAC No. 154/17 page 5 of 7 SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date:
2025.10.08 14:32:10 +0530 that he was not awarded sufficient compensation for same.
Accordingly, I hold that petitioner is not entitled to any enhancement in compensation on this count.

Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other statutory benefits under the LA Act viz. 12%
additional amount [as per section 23 (1A)] and 30% solatium [u/s 23 (2)] and will be entitled to interest under Section 28 of L.A Act on the fair market value @ 9% per annum for the first year and @ 15% for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.
Issue no. 1 is decided accordingly.
16. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF

The share(s) of the petitioner(s) would be determinable as per the statement u/s 19 of the L.A.
Act proved on record and the said statement shall constitute a part of this award.
18. Reference petition stands answered.
Parties to bear their own costs.
A copy of this award be sent to the LAC for necessary information, action and expeditious compliance for remittance of the amount.
File be consigned to record room.

Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other statutory benefits under the LA Act viz. 12%
additional amount [as per section 23 (1A)] and 30% solatium [u/s 23 (2)] and will be entitled to interest under Section 28 of L.A Act on the fair market value @ 9% per annum for the first year and @ 15% for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.

16. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF
In view of the findings on Issue no.1, the petitioner/s are granted the following reliefs: -
1. fair market value @ Rs.27,000/- per square meter for the acquired land as per statement u/s 19 of the LA Act;
2. additional amount @ 12% per annum on the fair market value u/s 23 (1A) of the LA Act, from the date of notification u/s 4 of the LA Act till the date of award or dispossession, whichever is earlier ;
3. solatium u/s 23(2) of LA Act @ 30% on the LAC No. 154/17 page 6 of 7 SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date:
2025.10.08 14:32:16 +0530 enhanced amount of compensation ;
4. interest under Section 28 of L.A Act @ 9% per annum for the first year from the date of dispossession and at the rate of 15% per annum on the difference between the enhanced compensation awarded by this court and the compensation awarded by the LAC for the subsequent period till its payment ;
17.
